wave_title: Persistence and Recovery Semantics -- bootstrap materialize the PERSISTENCE dimension (.atlas/contracts/SEMANTIC-FACTS.md#persistencefact, .atlas/roadmap/SELF-BUILDING-R4-R8.md R4.11): durable read/write/commit/rollback/checkpoint/recovery relationships and durable resource identity. This record covers the design-guard pass performed BEFORE implementation (deciding the canonical place/location boundary) and the resulting kernel/extractor/graph/multi-extractor wiring.

identity.candidate_state: uncommitted working tree on branch claude/r4-semantic-materialization-jz2z44, descended from PR #27's own tip (not yet merged at the time this record was written -- PR #27 remains open, base_commit_sha above is that PR's own HEAD)
identity.note: PR #27 (R4.4-R4.10 second hardening pass) was not yet merged when this R4.11 work began. Per explicit operator instruction ('work on the correct intended base... do not duplicate already-landed fixes'), R4.11 was built directly on top of PR #27's own branch tip rather than waiting or rebasing onto a stale pre-hardening main, since R4.11's design guard explicitly depends on that hardening pass's dimension_coverage mechanism and OwnershipResolution precedent.

design_guard_pass.question: Is the repository ready for a first-class PlaceIdentity shared by DATA_FLOW/STATE/OWNERSHIP/PERSISTENCE, or does R4.11 need the smaller bridge instead?

identity_landscape_before_implementing.DATA_FLOW: ValueIdentity, keyed by (function, name, span, role); a resolved Use/Store carries resolved_definition: Option<SemanticRecordId>, a real typed cross-reference to the Definition record -- the most mature existing 'place' concept, though scoped to local bindings only.
identity_landscape_before_implementing.STATE: StateAccessIdentity, keyed by (function, scope, name, kind); converges same-named self.field accesses onto one content-derived StateEntity graph node. Safe (unlike the OWNERSHIP bug below) because `name` always comes from self_field_ident(), a genuinely resolved field-access pattern, never an arbitrary temporary's spelling -- re-confirmed this pass, not merely assumed.
identity_landscape_before_implementing.OWNERSHIP: OwnershipIdentity, keyed by (function, name, span, kind) plus OwnershipResolution (Resolved/Unresolved), added in the immediately-prior hardening pass after a real bug: the engineering graph derived a target node id from (function, name) where name could be an UNRESOLVED TEMPORARY's raw spelling, letting two independent `&foo()` temporaries collapse onto one graph node.
identity_landscape_before_implementing.conclusion: Three independently-shaped mechanisms already exist. A full shared PlaceIdentity replacing all three would be a genuinely large, cross-cutting migration (touches core::semantic::{data_flow,state,ownership} and every consumer simultaneously, breaking three already-shipped identity_key() shapes) -- correctly evaluated and deferred as TARGET in the prior hardening pass's own evidence record, re-confirmed rather than re-litigated this pass.

design_guard_pass.decision: Built the smallest correct bridge instead of faking full convergence: PlaceRef (core::semantic::persistence) -- Resolved { dimension, record_id } | Unresolved. PersistenceIdentity.place: PlaceRef is deliberately excluded from identity_key() (matches OwnershipIdentity's resolution / ValueIdentity's resolved_definition precedent exactly).
design_guard_pass.convergence_proven_not_merely_designed: core::graph::engineering_graph::tests::resolved_persistence_place_converges_on_the_existing_state_access_node constructs a PERSISTENCE observation whose PlaceRef::Resolved names a STATE observation's own record_id, and asserts the graph draws its REFERS_TO_PLACE edge at the EXACT SAME node id STATE's own projection arm produced (via a new place_node_id_for(dimension, record_id) helper reconstructing that dimension's node-id prefix scheme) -- not a new, independently-invented node. This is the concrete falsification proving the bridge works, not just documentation asserting it does.
design_guard_pass.identity_debt_introduced: NO -- PlaceRef never derives identity from source spelling (game.commit() and wal.commit() produce identically-shaped Unresolved candidates); it never invents a new target node when Unresolved (unlike the fixed OWNERSHIP bug, there is no place-target node at all in that case, so nothing can collapse); and it reuses existing dimensions' own canonical identities via cross-reference rather than duplicating them.

persistence_model.kernel: core/src/semantic/persistence.rs: PersistenceKind (12 variants: Commit/Flush/Sync/Checkpoint/Snapshot emitted this wave; JournalAppend/DurableRead/DurableWrite/TransactionBegin/TransactionAbort/Recover/Restore declared, never emitted), PersistenceResolution (Resolved/Unresolved), PlaceRef (the bridge, see design_guard_pass above), PersistenceIdentity { repository, revision, function, kind, span, place, resolution }.
persistence_model.scope_this_wave: No dedicated Rust syntax for persistence exists (unlike R4.10's `.await`), and no resolved-API adapter exists yet, so every PersistenceKind this wave materializes is a textual callee-spelling candidate ONLY (Call and MethodCall receivers/functions whose last path/method segment is exactly commit/flush/sync/sync_all/sync_data/checkpoint/snapshot), exactly R4.8's is_panic_like_macro / R4.10's is_spawn_call risk class. Always EpistemicStatus::Inferred, PersistenceResolution::Unresolved, PlaceRef::Unresolved -- never Observed, never a resolved place, regardless of how 'real' the receiver looks.
persistence_model.walker_coverage: adapter/src/semantic/rust/persistence.rs's PersistenceWalker was built with full expression-tree coverage from the start (Unsafe/Const/Repeat/RawAddr/TryBlock/Yield all walked; Closure/Async explicitly excluded as deferred regions), learning directly from the prior hardening pass's finding that CALL/DATA_FLOW/OWNERSHIP/CONCURRENCY initially shipped without this coverage and needed a follow-up fix -- PERSISTENCE does not repeat that mistake.

closure_status.implementation: bootstrap materialized -- conservative textual-spelling-only candidate detection, with the PlaceRef bridge wired end-to-end (kernel, extractor, graph projection, multi-extractor preservation).
closure_status.coverage_profile: Partial (see dimension_coverage in adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs, now covering all 8 full-expression-tree dimensions including PERSISTENCE): shares the macro-invocation-argument-opacity gap every other full-tree walker has, and additionally has no dedicated syntax at all (unlike CONCURRENCY's `.await`) and no resolved-API adapter.
closure_status.closure: OPEN -- dimension obligation remains UNKNOWN even when real candidates exist; zero observations are never verified absence (falsified directly: cargo run systemize against this repository's own source found zero real commit/flush/sync/checkpoint/snapshot method calls -- independently confirmed by grep -- and the resulting PERSISTENCE obligation for every artifact is UNKNOWN with an IncompleteAnalysis diagnostic, never fabricated Observed absence).
known_gaps: no dedicated syntax evidence source at all (fundamental to Rust, not a bootstrap limitation)

no resolved-API adapter yet for std::fs::File::sync_all, database transaction commit APIs, WAL append APIs, snapshot APIs, etc. -- PersistenceResolution::Resolved is a real code path (tested directly in core::semantic::persistence's own unit tests) but never reached by the current Rust extractor

durability ordering (write -> flush -> commit) and recovery-relation semantics (restore recovers-from checkpoint/journal) not yet modeled -- PlaceRef gives operations a shared location reference but no ordering/graph-edge semantics between two PERSISTENCE operations themselves
no connection yet to FailureScenario/VerificationWorld/obligation/evidence from VERIFICATION-METRICS-PERFORMANCE.md -- documented as a TARGET relationship in the roadmap, not implemented this pass
PlaceRef itself is an explicit BRIDGE, not the TARGET first-class PlaceIdentity shared natively by all four dimensions

cross_dimension_consistency_proven.invariant: a bare STATE mutation never fabricates a durable PERSISTENCE fact
an unrelated method merely spelled like a persistence operation (game.commit()) is treated identically to a real one -- both only Inferred, never Observed
two identically-spelled operations at different sites remain distinct, never collapsed (the R4.9 OwnershipTarget lesson, re-applied and re-tested for a new dimension)
a persistence-shaped call inside a nested closure/async block is never attributed to the enclosing function
a Resolved PlaceRef converges on the SAME graph node an existing dimension's own observation produced -- proven, not merely asserted
an Unresolved PlaceRef produces no place-target node/edge at all -- the safest possible choice, no new spelling-collapse risk

multi_extractor_and_graph_proof.claim: Two independent extractors reporting the identical Persistence claim both survive Census and Normalization; the engineering graph preserves EpistemicStatus/PersistenceResolution as node attributes.
